answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake that vests over time, like a terrace built level by level: a newcomer may observe and do small jobs, but high-value work unlocks only after sustained honest behavior. Creating many fake accounts then costs real capital per identity, and misbehavior burns the stake - like pigment that stains every copy - so a Sybil farmer's orchard of sockpuppets withers instead of scaling, since each fake must pay full price and risks losing it.
